title: (No AI) China’s Alibaba takes another swipe at America’s AI supremacy
author: Robert Hart
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/gettyimages-2266883826.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

The Alibaba logo is displayed outside its headquarters in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China. | Image: NurPhoto via Getty Images

Chinese tech giant Alibaba released what it says is its largest and "most capable AI model to date," claiming performance rivaling the best systems from US frontier labs Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as domestic rivals like Moonshot AI's Kimi K3. Alibaba said it was making the model, Qwen3.8-Max, widely available to users in a [blog post](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen3.8) published on Monday. The release had been expected after the company [previewed](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/967781/chinese-ai-models-open-source-moonshot-kimi-k3-alibaba-qwen) the model last month, when it claimed it was "second only to Fable 5," Anthropic's flagship.

The open release of another highly capable Chinese AI model adds to [sky-high tensions](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/972380/open-ai-hugging-face-hack-ai-safety-warning) along multiple fronts in Silicon Valley and Washin …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/974342/alibaba-qwen-max-open-weight-ai)

title: (No AI) Fender’s CEO seems to think your bandmates are just analog AI
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/gettyimages-1259130896.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Edward “Bud” Cole speaks in Japan in 2023. | Image: Jun Sato/WireImage

Fender CEO Edward "Bud" Cole gave an interview to [_T3_](https://www.t3.com/home-living/welcome-to-tele-town-fender-celebrates-75-years-of-the-telecaster) in May celebrating the 75th anniversary of the Telecaster with comments on AI and music that initially flew under the radar. But it has started [making the rounds](https://guitar.com/news/industry-news/fender-ceo-defends-ai/) [recently](https://www.guitarworld.com/artists/guitarists/fender-ceo-bud-cole-ai-comments), pouring more fuel on an already raging fire of bad PR following the company [pissing off](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OU7RUpkXsV0) [basically](https://youtu.be/BOv8HD4LklY) the [entire](https://youtu.be/FXdGYqlLugE) guitar-playing [community](https://youtu.be/l4x1oHfu8w0) by [sending](https://youtu.be/vUIRZz5BbUY) [cease-and-desist](https://youtu.be/18Np7TmKbS0) letters to builders, claiming copyright of the Stratocaster body shape.

Some influential guitar YouTubers have even said they're [done buying Fender gear](https://youtu.be/tK32zkbWOMc) in the wake of the controversy. And Cole's resurfaced comments comparing cover songs and bandmates to a sort …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/974265/fender-ceo-bud-cole-ai-music)
